paper.title: A Smoothed Analysis of the Greedy Algorithm for the Linear Contextual Bandit Problem

settings.name_in_paper: Single parameter setting against the sigma-perturbed adversary
unmapped: Contexts: an adaptive adversary picks k means in the unit ball each round, then each is perturbed by independent N(0, sigma^2 I) Gaussian noise (smoothed analysis)
Single shared parameter beta with ||beta|| <= 1 across all k arms
settings.definition_quote: There is a single unknown vector \b \in \R^d. In round t, contexts x_1^t,...,x_k^t are presented... The learner chooses an arm i^t and obtains s-subgaussian reward ... E[r] = \b \cdot x_{i^t}^t ... First, an adaptive adversary picks the contexts arbitrarily from the unit ball. Then each context is perturbed independently by draws from a Gaussian with mean 0 and variance \sigma^2.

settings.name_in_paper: Single parameter setting against an R-bounded, centrally bounded, diverse perturbed adversary
unmapped: Contexts = adaptive adversarial means in unit ball plus mean-zero perturbations from general distributions satisfying (r,lambda_0)-diversity and (r,1/T)-central boundedness, with ||x|| <= R a.s.
settings.definition_quote: We use perturbed adversary to refer to the same process, but where the perturbations e_1^t,...,e_k^t may be drawn from different mean-zero distributions D_1^t,...,D_k^t, chosen possibly as a function of h^t.

settings.name_in_paper: Multiple parameter setting against the sigma-perturbed adversary (with warm start)
unmapped: Each arm i has its own unknown parameter beta_i in R^d with ||beta_i|| <= 1 (disjoint linear models)
Contexts: adaptive adversarial means in the unit ball perturbed by independent N(0, sigma^2 I) Gaussian noise
Learner receives a warm start of n (perturbed) samples per arm before the T rounds
settings.definition_quote:
There are $k$ unknown vectors
  $\bi{1},\ldots,\bi{k} \in \R^d$.  In round $t$, contexts
  $\pxit{1}{t},\ldots, \pxit{k}{t}$ are presented, with each
  $\pxit{i}{t} \in \R^d$. The learner chooses an arm
  $i^t \in \{1,\ldots,k\}$, and obtains $s$-subgaussian reward
  $\rit{i^t}{t}$ such that
  $\E{\rit{i^t}{t}} = \bi{i^t} \cdot \pxit{i^t}{t}$.

Warm start of n samples per arm

source.label: thm:singleparam-conditions-regret
source.quote: Consider a single-parameter perturbed adversary that is R-bounded and (r, \frac{1}{T})-centrally-bounded and (r,\lambda_0)-diverse for some r \leq R\leq \mathrm{polylog}(T). If the reward noise is s-subgaussian for constant s\geq 1, then with probability 1-\delta, Greedy suffers regret \text{Regret}(T) \leq \frac{32 R^{3/2} \sqrt{T d s \ln(2T k d/\delta)}}{\lambda_0}

results.notes: This is the conference-version (\else branch) statement of the same theorem label; constant differs from Theorem 3.1.

source.label: thm:singleparam-perturbed-regret
source.quote: In the single parameter setting against the \sigma-perturbed adversary \Asig, with probability 1-\delta, for fixed s (rewards' subgaussian parameter) and k (number of arms) and \sigma \leq O\left(\left(\sqrt{d\ln(Tkd/\delta)}\right)^{-1}\right), Greedy has \text{Regret}(T) \leq O\left( \frac{\sqrt{T d s} \left(\ln\frac{Td}{\delta}\right)^{3/2}} {\sigma^2} \right).

results.notes: No warm start needed. Lemma 3.8 / Lemma B.2 give same bound for truncated adversary and a large-sigma regime bound O(d^2 sqrt(Ts) ln^3 / sqrt(sigma)) for the truncated adversary (not recorded separately).

source.label: thm:multiparam-conditions-regret
source.quote: Consider an R-bounded, (r,\frac{1}{T})-centrally, (r,\lambda_0)-diverse perturbed adversary with (r,\alpha,\gamma) margins. If the warm start size n \geq n^*(\delta/2), where n^*(\delta/2) is defined in Lemma \ref{lemma:multi-warm-convergence}, then with probability 1-\delta, \text{Regret}(T) \leq \frac{192 R^{3/2} \sqrt{6Tdks} \left(\ln\frac{4Tdk}{\delta}\right)^{3/2}}{\gamma \lambda_0}.

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: Suppose greedy is given a warm start of size n \leq \left(\frac{1}{100 \sigma^2\ln \frac{\rho}{100}}\right) in a \sigma-perturbed instance for some \rho. Then, there exists an instance for which Greedy incurs regret \Omega( \frac{\rho}{\sqrt{n}} ) with constant probability in its first \rho rounds.

results.notes: Lower bound specific to Greedy; 'with constant probability' recorded as realized regret. Shows warm start must be poly(1/sigma) to avoid linear regret.

source.label: thm:lower-difference
source.quote: Let \epsilon = \min_i |\bi{i}|, \sigma < \frac{1}{\sqrt{\ln \frac{T}{\delta}}} and \frac{T}{\delta} < 2^{n^{1/3}}. Suppose Greedy is given a warm start of size n \leq \frac{1}{2\epsilon}. Then, there is an instance which causes Greedy to incur expected regret \Omega \left(\epsilon \left(e^{\frac{1}{ 18\sigma^2}} - n^{2/3}\right)\right).

results.notes: Paper calls it expected regret; regret is defined through means, so recorded as pseudo-regret. Proof is informal and the instance parameters are inconsistent between the text and the proof.
